name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.NonUnitalCStarRepresentation.IsSingletonIrreducibleModel
title: A representative of the unique irreducible class

content.display_title: A representative of the unique irreducible class
content.one_sentence_role: Defines when one nonzero irreducible $*$-representation represents the sole unitary-equivalence class of such representations.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a complex $C^*$-algebra, with no unit assumed, and let $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ be a $*$-representation. The predicate below says that $\pi$ is nonzero irreducible and that every other nonzero irreducible $*$-representation of $A$ is unitarily equivalent to $\pi$.
content.definition_explanation: Require first that $\pi$ act nontrivially and have no proper nonzero closed reducing subspace. Then, for every complex Hilbert space $K$ and every nonzero irreducible $*$-representation $\rho:A\to\mathcal B(K)$, require a unitary operator $U:H\to K$ such that $$U\pi(a)=\rho(a)U\qquad(a\in A).$$
content.assumptions: No separability or faithfulness condition is part of this definition. The algebra may be unital, but the definition does not require a unit or a unit-preservation equation.
content.conclusion: The output is a property of the specified $\pi$: it represents the unique unitary-equivalence class of nonzero irreducible $*$-representations of $A$.
lean_realization_notes: Faithfulness is not part of this definition. Later theorems impose hypotheses to deduce it. “Non-unital” permits an algebra with a unit; it does not assert that a unit fails to exist.
